bss.topic: Estrutura da Terra e placas tectônicas

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual é a camada mais externa da Terra, onde vivemos?
questions.hint: É a camada mais fina, como a casca de uma fruta.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual é a camada mais central e mais quente da Terra?
questions.hint: Pense no "caroço" do planeta.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual camada da Terra fica entre a crosta e o núcleo?
questions.hint: É a camada mais grossa, de rocha muito quente.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Como é o núcleo externo da Terra?
options: Líquido, formado principalmente por ferro e níquel
questions.answer: Líquido, formado principalmente por ferro e níquel
questions.hint: O núcleo interno é sólido; o externo é diferente.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: O que são placas tectônicas?
options: Grandes blocos da litosfera que se movem lentamente
questions.answer: Grandes blocos da litosfera que se movem lentamente
questions.hint: A superfície da Terra é dividida como um quebra-cabeça.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Em qual placa tectônica está todo o território do Brasil?
questions.hint: O nome da placa lembra o continente.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Por que o Brasil tem poucos terremotos fortes?
options: Porque fica no meio de uma placa, longe das bordas
Porque está perto da Linha do Equador
questions.answer: Porque fica no meio de uma placa, longe das bordas
questions.hint: Pense em onde as placas se encontram.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Onde acontece a maioria dos terremotos e vulcões do planeta?
questions.hint: É onde as placas se empurram, se afastam ou deslizam.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: A Cordilheira dos Andes se formou pelo encontro de quais placas?
options: Placa de Nazca e Placa Sul-Americana
Placa do Pacífico e Placa Antártica
questions.answer: Placa de Nazca e Placa Sul-Americana
questions.hint: Os Andes ficam no oeste da América do Sul, perto do Oceano Pacífico.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Comparada à crosta continental, a crosta oceânica é:
questions.hint: Embaixo dos oceanos a "casca" da Terra é diferente.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: O que faz as placas tectônicas se moverem?
questions.hint: O calor de dentro da Terra movimenta a rocha quente do manto.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual é o nome do supercontinente que reunia todos os continentes há cerca de 200 milhões de anos?
questions.hint: O nome vem do grego e significa "toda a terra".

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual é a velocidade aproximada do movimento das placas tectônicas?
questions.hint: É mais ou menos a velocidade com que suas unhas crescem.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Num limite divergente, as placas:
questions.hint: "Divergir" quer dizer ir para lados opostos.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual frase sobre terremotos no Brasil é verdadeira?
options: São os mais fortes do mundo
questions.hint: Mesmo no meio de uma placa há pequenos tremores.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Explique por que o Chile tem muito mais terremotos do que o Brasil, usando a ideia de placas tectônicas.
questions.hint: Compare onde cada país fica em relação às bordas das placas.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Why do computers use binary?
options: Their circuits have two states: on and off
It uses less electricity to count to ten
questions.answer: Their circuits have two states: on and off
questions.hint: Think about what a switch can do.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: What is a single binary digit (a 0 or a 1) called?
questions.hint: It is short for "binary digit".

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Binary is a number system with base:
questions.hint: Count how many different digits binary uses.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Convert the binary number 101 to denary.
questions.hint: Use the place values 4, 2 and 1.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Convert the binary number 1010 to denary.
questions.hint: Use the place values 8, 4, 2 and 1.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: In binary, which number comes straight after 0111?
questions.hint: Add 1 and carry, just like 0999 + 1 in denary.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Write the denary number 6 in binary using 3 bits.
questions.hint: Which of 4, 2 and 1 add up to 6?

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Convert the binary number 1111 to denary.
questions.hint: Add up all four place values.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Write the denary number 9 in binary using 4 bits.
questions.hint: Which of 8, 4, 2 and 1 add up to 9?

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: How many different values can be stored using 3 bits?
questions.hint: Each extra bit doubles the number of patterns.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: How many bits are there in one byte?
questions.hint: It is the same as the number of values 3 bits can make.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: What are the place values of a 4-bit binary number, from left to right?
questions.hint: Each place is double the one to its right.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Convert the binary number 10000 to denary.
questions.hint: The fifth place value is double 8.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Write the denary number 12 in binary using 4 bits.
questions.hint: Start with the biggest place value that fits.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Convert the binary number 11001 to denary.
questions.hint: The place values are 16, 8, 4, 2 and 1.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Explain why it is easier for an electronic circuit to store binary than denary.
questions.hint: How many different states would a circuit need for denary?

en.topic: Non-fiction writing: purpose, audience and form

questions.subject: en
questions.q: In non-fiction writing, what does "purpose" mean?
options: The reason the text was written
The people who will read the text
questions.answer: The reason the text was written
questions.hint: Ask: why did the writer write it?

questions.subject: en
questions.q: What does "audience" mean when we talk about a text?
options: The people the text is written for
The main idea of the text
questions.answer: The people the text is written for
questions.hint: Ask: who is it for?

questions.subject: en
questions.q: What does "form" mean when we talk about a text?
options: The type of text, such as a letter or leaflet
questions.answer: The type of text, such as a letter or leaflet
questions.hint: Ask: what kind of text is it?

questions.subject: en
questions.q: A leaflet saying "Visit Sunny Bay Zoo this summer – you won't regret it!" is mainly written to:
questions.hint: The writer wants you to do something.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: What is the main purpose of a recipe?
questions.hint: It tells you how to make something step by step.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which form is most suitable for complaining to a company about a broken product?
questions.hint: The reader is a business, not a friend.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: What word describes the attitude or feeling created by a writer's choice of words, for example formal, chatty or serious?
questions.hint: We use the same word for the sound of someone's voice.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which opening is most suitable for a guide about brushing teeth written for 6-year-olds?
options: Did you know your teeth love a good brush?
Oral care is an obligation for all citizens.
questions.answer: Did you know your teeth love a good brush?
questions.hint: Young children need simple, friendly words.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which sentence is the most formal way to say "Hey, the trip was awesome!"?
options: The school trip was a great success.
Wow, what a cool trip, guys!
questions.answer: The school trip was a great success.
questions.hint: Formal writing avoids slang and exclamations.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Imperative verbs such as "Mix", "Turn" and "Press" are a key feature of which kind of text?
questions.hint: These verbs tell the reader what to do.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: What is the name for a non-fiction text that tells the story of a real person's life, written by someone else?
questions.hint: If the person writes it themselves, it has "auto" at the start.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Why might a writer use a rhetorical question in a persuasive speech?
options: To make the audience think and agree
To give exact facts and figures
questions.answer: To make the audience think and agree
questions.hint: The writer does not expect a real answer.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Who is the most likely audience for a magazine article called "10 Easy Skateboard Tricks for Beginners"?
options: Young people who are new to skateboarding
questions.answer: Young people who are new to skateboarding
questions.hint: Look closely at the words "easy" and "beginners".

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which feature would you expect in a newspaper report?
options: A headline and the 5 Ws (who, what, where, when, why)
questions.answer: A headline and the 5 Ws (who, what, where, when, why)
questions.hint: Think about what you see at the top of a news story.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Rewrite this sentence for a formal report to parents: "Our canteen serves loads of yummy grub."
questions.hint: Replace the slang with standard, polite words.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: A road safety leaflet is written for 7-year-olds and another for adults. Give two ways the writing would be different.
questions.hint: Think about vocabulary, sentence length and pictures or tone.
